bounded_question: How does node #115 build the OptionTypeInfo record for a custom shared_ptr SystemClock option, and how do the record's two create hooks resolve that option by name?

fields.name: padding
fields.note: never written by the builder or by the copy helper; its content is indeterminate

fields.name: type
fields.note: the custom-shared-ptr kind this builder writes

builder.stack_temp: The builder first fills an identical 0xb8-byte record as a stack temporary at rsp+0x20 (offset at temp+0x00, hooks at temp+0x18, type 22 at temp+0xa8, verification at temp+0xac, flags at temp+0xb0) and then installs it into out with the record-copy helper 0x5e332c0 (site 0x5fd0266, args (out, temp)). The hook pair is also staged at rsp+0x10 (temp-0x10) as the temporary's std::function object, whose manager the builder destroys after the copy.

manager_destroy.effect: No-op: op 3 is destroy_functor and the lambda captures nothing, so the manager returns 0 without touching memory. Skipped when the manager pointer at rsp+0x10 is null.

record_dtor.effect: No-op for the freshly built record: the destructor destroys the functor members at record+0x58/+0x78/+0x98 via their managers with op 3 when non-null, and all three are zero here. Cited by contract (FDE 0x5d3f950..0x5d3f9d3); not excerpted.

copy_helper.role: OptionTypeInfo copy-assignment: copies a 0xb8-byte record from rsi into rdi. The record holds five std::function members at +0x08/+0x28/+0x48/+0x68/+0x88 (each 0x20 bytes: functor storage at +0x00, manager at +0x10, invoker at +0x18).
steps: Copy the 4-byte offset at +0x00; zero out+0x08..+0x18 and out+0x18/+0x20.

For each of the five members (in order +0x08, +0x28, +0x48, +0x68, +0x88): zero the member in out; when the source member's manager (at member+0x10) is non-null, call manager(out+member, src+member, op 2 = clone_functor) and then copy the manager+invoker pair (16 bytes) from the source member.
Copy the 8 bytes at +0xa8 (type + verification) and the 4 bytes at +0xb0 (flags) verbatim.
copy_helper.landing_pads: The five endbr64 stubs at 0x5e33438..0x5e3354d each save %rax and destroy the already-copied members in reverse order via their managers with op 3, then resume unwinding via _Unwind_Resume; not decoded beyond that shape.
copy_helper.note: Shared by every OptionTypeInfo installer in the binary (85 direct call sites, including the SliceTransform sibling builder's site 0x6083b76). The Statistics sibling builder 0x6071520 (open PR #3685) does NOT call it: it copies field-wise and calls the manager directly instead. For this builder only the first member is non-empty (the create hooks); the other four members are all zero, so their clones are skipped.

manager.role: std::function manager (_Function_handler manager) for the AsCustomSharedPtr<SystemClock> lambda. Reached only through the GOT slot 0x64ed8d0 and the copy helper's indirect manager call; it has no direct call site.

ops.name: get_type_info
ops.effect: *(out) = 0x64cda00, the address of the lambda typeinfo object (vtable __cxxabiv1::__class_type_info + 0x10, name string at 0x972460)

ops.name: clone_functor
ops.effect: no-op, returns 0 (empty lambda: nothing to copy)

ops.name: destroy_functor
ops.effect: no-op, returns 0 (empty lambda: nothing to free)

invoker.role: std::function _M_invoke for the AsCustomSharedPtr<SystemClock> lambda: Status (const ConfigOptions&, const std::string&, const std::string&, void*), returned through a hidden sret pointer in rdi. Reached only through the GOT slot 0x64ed958; it has no direct call site.

args.config_options: rdx (passed to the create host as its 2nd arg)
args.dest_slot: r9 (pointer to the destination shared_ptr slot)

id_fast_path.condition: id_string length == 2 and its first two bytes are 'id' (word 0x6469) and name_string length == 0
id_fast_path.effect: Release the shared_ptr at *(dest_slot): zero the 16-byte slot, then call _M_release 0x5d350c0 (site 0x5fd4ca1) on the old control block when non-null (the packed use/weak fast path and the use-count decrement live inside _M_release itself, pinned by open PR #3674 — unlike the Statistics invoker, this invoker does not inline them). Then write an empty Status (code 0, subcode 0, state null) to out and return out.

create_host.role: Create-by-name host for the SystemClock option: resolves the name against the current clock, adopting it when it matches, and otherwise creates the default clock through the registry translator. Pinned here for the first time.

current_clock.load: r15 = *(control+0x00) = the clock object (object+0x10 of the combined allocation); rbp = *(control+0x08) = the control block (the allocation base).
current_clock.use_count_bump: The use count at control+0x08 is bumped by 1: lock addl when the global byte at 0x64ed290 is 0, plain addl otherwise (sites 0x5fd4715 / 0x5fd4978).

name_dispatch.detail: Read vtable slot 0x80 of the current clock's table (0x64ce930) and compare it with the global at 0x64eceb8 (RELATIVE -> 0x5d2e770, the default implementation, FDE 0x5d2e770..0x5d2e832). When they differ, call slot 0x80 (current, name); a false result goes to the default path. When they are equal, the predicate is skipped and the host does the same matching inline (steps below). The default predicate itself is verified by reading its body: it returns false for an empty input name; otherwise it returns true when the input equals the slot-0x70 name (strlen + memcmp) or, failing that, the slot-0x90 name (null -> false; strlen + memcmp); otherwise false.
When name_string length is 0, go to the default path.
Call vtable slot 0x70 (current) for its name string; when strlen(name) == name_string length and memcmp is 0, adopt the current clock. Otherwise fall through to the slot 0x90 check.

Read vtable slot 0x90 and compare it with the global at 0x64eceb0 (RELATIVE -> 0x5d2ca10, the default implementation, FDE 0x5d2ca10..0x5d2ca1c: 7 bytes, lea of the empty string at 0x4376fd and ret — the default second name is empty). When they are equal, go to the default path. When they differ, call slot 0x90 (current) for a second name string; when it is non-null and strlen(name) == name_string length and memcmp is 0, adopt the current clock; otherwise go to the default path.

adopt_path.effect: Install the current clock into *dest_slot: write the object pointer at dest+0x00 and the control block at dest+0x08; when the old control differs from the new one, bump the new control's use count (same 0x64ed290 selector rule) and release the old control via _M_release 0x5d350c0 (site 0x5fd49c3). Then write an empty Status to out.

default_path.once_init: pthread_once with the once control at 0x6504b68, the initializer 0x5fd20d0 (passed by lea at 0x5fd47c1) and the TLS slots 0x64ed818/0x64ed820/0x64ed828; on pthread_once failure the host throws a system error (site 0x5fd4beb).
default_path.translator: Call the registry translator 0x609e510 (site 0x5fd489a; by contract, open PR #3440) with a stack-built options struct (Status out at rsp+0x20, config_options, *dest_slot object, name_string, translated-name string at rsp+0x90, once-arg at rsp+0x50). The translator writes a Status at rsp+0x20, the translated name into the string at rsp+0x90 (length at rsp+0x98) and an error out-param at rsp+0x68.

outcomes.effect: out = move(translator Status) via the Status move helper 0x5fcdf70 (site 0x5fd48c6).

outcomes.condition: translator Status code == 0 and the translated name is non-empty
outcomes.effect: Call the name-to-clock factory helper 0x5fd4080 (site 0x5fd4aa3; by contract, FDE 0x5fd4080..0x5fd4627) with (Status out at rsp+0x40, config_options+0x40, the translated name string, dest_slot), then normalize the resulting Status (see status_normalization) and move it to out.

outcomes.condition: translator Status code == 0, translated name empty, error out-param (rsp+0x68) non-null
outcomes.effect: Build an error Status via the Status builder 0x61cf670 (site 0x5fd4bc9; by contract, open PR #3440) with code 3 and the message at 0x433f9f ("Cannot reset object ") plus the name at 0x4376fd, then move it to out.

outcomes.condition: translator Status code == 0, translated name empty, error out-param null
outcomes.effect: Release *dest_slot (zero the 16-byte slot, _M_release the old control via site 0x5fd4955) and write an empty Status to out.

status_normalization.input: the factory helper's Status, moved to rsp+0x30
rules: code == 3 (NotSupported, per RocksDB's Status code table — inference) and config_options+1 != 0: reset the intermediate Status to empty; out = empty.
code == 0: call the second translator 0x609e2d0 (site 0x5fd4b76; by contract) with (rsp+0x40, config_options, *dest_slot object, current clock), then move the Status at rsp+0x40 to rsp+0x30 and out.
any other code: out = the factory Status unchanged.
status_normalization.note: The config_options+1 byte's meaning and the 0x609e2d0 contract are open; only the branch structure is pinned.

cleanup.effect: Free the array at rsp+0x28 (operator delete[] when non-null); call the once-arg cleanup helper 0x5d36110 (site 0x5fd48dd; by contract, FDE 0x5d36110..0x5d361d5) on rsp+0x50; dispose the translated-name string via _M_dispose (site 0x5fd48e7); release the local current-clock reference via _M_release 0x5d350c0 when non-null (site 0x5fd48f4); stack-canary check; return out.

accessor.role: Function-local-static accessor for the current SystemClock shared_ptr (guard byte at 0x6504c98, static at 0x6504ca0). Called from ~190 sites across the node; only the create host's use is pinned in detail here.
accessor.fast_path: When the guard byte is set, return the static's value (the control-block pointer).
slow_path: __cxa_guard_acquire on the guard; when another thread is initializing, return the static's value.
Allocate the 0x10-byte control block (operator new) and the 0x30-byte combined allocation (operator new).

Combined allocation layout: control block at +0x00..+0x10 (table 0x64ced00, packed counts qword 0x100000001 at +0x08, copied from the global at 0x459b20) and the PosixClock object at +0x10..+0x30 (table 0x64ce930 at +0x00, zeroes at +0x08/+0x10/+0x18).
Control block at +0x00: object+0x10; at +0x08: the allocation base. Store the control block in the static at 0x6504ca0; __cxa_guard_release; return the control block.
accessor.clock_identity: The object table 0x64ce930 resolves (via the RELATIVE record at 0x64ce928) to the typeinfo at 0x64ce870, whose name string at 0x972c00 is rocksdb::(anonymous)::PosixClock; the control table 0x64ced00 resolves (via the RELATIVE record at 0x64cecf8) to the typeinfo at 0x64ce8b8, std::_Sp_counted_ptr_inplace<PosixClock, ...>. The packed counts 0x100000001 mean use 1, weak 1. The vtable-header cells in this binary carry the typeinfo pointer at base-0x08 (verified on five vtables: StatisticsImpl, HistogramImpl, SystemClockWrapper, PosixClock, _Sp_counted_ptr_inplace<PosixClock>); slot numbers in this packet are relative to the stored table base, as the code reads them.
accessor.control_vtable_slots: Read at the stored control-table base 0x64ced00: slot +0x10 is _M_dispose 0x5fe1860, slot +0x18 is _M_destroy 0x5fe1590 (operator delete, size 0x30), slot +0x20 is _M_get_deleter 0x5fe15a0 — the slots _M_release calls.

default_init.role: pthread_once initializer for the default SystemClock registry entry (the routine the create host passes to pthread_once by lea at 0x5fd47c1). It has no direct call site; it is reached only through pthread_once.
steps: Build a stack string via the string helper 0x5fcd890 (by contract) from the literal "TimeEmulatedSystemClock" at 0x4372ae.
Fetch the registry mutex via 0x61f8b60 (by contract; returns the mutex pointer, saved to r12).
Build a second stack object at rsp+0x60 via 0x5fcd890 with the table references 0x5fcd550 / 0x5fcc630 (by contract).
Allocate the 0x30-byte registry entry (operator new) and the 0x70-byte clock object (operator new, table 0x64d8ec0+0x10, byte +0x48 = 1); link the entry to the clock object.

Lock the registry mutex; insert the entry into the mutex-guarded registry under the name "SystemClock" (literal at 0x438369) via the registry helper 0x5fd1da0 (site 0x5fd22b4; by contract); unlock; dispose the temporaries.
default_init.note: The registry structure and the 0x5fcd890 / 0x61f8b60 / 0x5fcd6f0 / 0x5fd1da0 / 0x61f8700 contracts are open; only the allocation sizes, the table pointers, the two name literals and the lock/insert/unlock shape are pinned. pthread_mutex_lock failure throws a system error; the landing pads are shared rethrow blocks (not decoded).

status_move.role: rocksdb::Status move-assignment (dst = std::move(src)). A shared helper (17 direct call sites); the create host uses it four times.
steps: When dst == src, return dst at once.
Copy bytes 0..5 from src to dst; zero src bytes 1..5 (src byte 0, the code, is left intact).
Move the state qword at +0x08 from src to dst, freeing dst's old state via operator delete[] when non-null; src state becomes null.
status_move.note: The 0x10-byte Status layout pinned here is: code byte at +0x00, subcode and severity bytes at +0x01..+0x05, state pointer (char*) at +0x08. An empty Status is all zeros.

factory_helper_contract.role: Name-to-clock factory helper: takes (Status out, config_options+0x40, translated-name string, dest_slot) and writes a Status to out. Its sole caller is the create host (site 0x5fd4aa3). Cited by contract only; its internals are not pinned here.

args.out: rdi (a stack Status at rsp+0x40 in the host)
args.name: rdx (the translated-name string)

installer.note: The containing function (0x5fd19a0..0x5fd1c56) is a static initializer: it registers __cxa_atexit for the global at 0x6504bc0, installs the record with the builder, then assigns the string "target" (literal at 0x44a390) via 0x5fcd890. It is NOT pinned here; only this call site and its arguments are. It is the builder's sole direct caller in the binary.

sibling_note.claim: The SystemClock builder shares the record field map with the Statistics builder 0x6071520 (open PR #3685) — same 0xb8-byte record, same type 22, same hook-pair layout — but installs it differently: this builder copies through the record-copy helper 0x5e332c0, while the Statistics builder copies field-wise and calls the manager directly. The GOT-resolved hooks prove SystemClock, not Statistics or FileSystem: the manager 0x5fcc660 is the SystemClock lambda manager (its kind-0 typeinfo name at 0x972460 is the AsCustomSharedPtr<SystemClock> lambda) and the invoker 0x5fd4c30 calls the SystemClock create host 0x5fd46c0.
sibling_note.other_sibling: The SliceTransform sibling builder 0x6083a90 shares this builder's install shape (it also calls the copy helper 0x5e332c0 — census site 0x6083b76) and resolves its own hooks through its own GOT slots (manager 0x607d190, invoker 0x60809e0; typeinfo name at 0x976100 is the AsCustomSharedPtr<const SliceTransform> lambda). It is a separate work item.

unknowns: The OptionVerificationType / OptionTypeFlags enum spellings for the raw values verification 1 / flags 0x2000 used by the sole installing call site; only the raw values are pinned.

The semantic names of the invoker's two string args beyond their observed roles (rcx is the string compared to "id", r8 is the name string the create host dispatches on); the lambda's mangled type only fixes their C++ types.

The exact vtable-base/header attribution of the PosixClock tables: the typeinfo-bearing cells sit at the stored base minus 0x08 in this binary (verified on five vtables), so slot numbers here are relative to the stored base as the code reads them; the -0x10 cell's role (0, except 0x7 for the PosixClock object table) is open.
The registry structure built by the default initializer (0x5fcd890 / 0x61f8b60 / 0x5fcd6f0 / 0x5fd1da0 / 0x61f8700 by contract) and the roles of the 0x5fcd550 / 0x5fcc630 table references inside it.
The factory helper 0x5fd4080's internals (by contract only).
The translator 0x609e510's stack struct layout beyond the pinned out-params (translated-name string at rsp+0x90, error out-param at rsp+0x68) and the second translator 0x609e2d0's contract.
The config_options+1 byte's meaning in the Status normalization branch.
Whether the "id" fast path means "reset to the default object" or "release and return empty" in the caller's terms; the binary only shows the release + empty Status.
The "target" string's role in the installer (assigned after the builder call).
The host's landing-pad stubs (FDE 0x5fd4c22..0x5fd4c2e region and the jumps to 0x5fd4646/0x5fd4680) are shared rethrow blocks, not decoded; the LSDA call-site tables are not decoded.
